lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Kell Village is not the village you left. By the gate there is a wall that was not there this morning: a hundred and sixty-four names from a winter in 2148, cut in four different hands, with a line of hand-forged blades hung above them. The market runs further down the lane than it did. Nobody is looking at the sky.

lines.speaker: dax
lines.text: They remember it. They remember us — there's a forge mark up there that's near enough my great-grandmother's. I'm not sure I like being a legend, Sister. Legends are what you get instead of people.

lines.speaker: wren
lines.text: You are not a legend. You are a wall of names a town chose to keep, and argued about keeping, and could have melted down for metal it needs, and did not. That is better than a legend. A legend is what happens when nobody can check.
